Bug Exploit refers to an attack that takes advantage of a flaw in smart contract or protocol code to drain funds or manipulate behavior. Bug Exploit is usually carried out by attackers who identify a vulnerability before its developers fix it. Bug Exploit can cause direct financial losses for users whose funds are held in the affected code.

Capitulation describes a market phase in which investors sell their holdings in panic after a prolonged decline in prices. Capitulation is characterized by heavy selling volume and a sharp drop in prices. Capitulation is sometimes viewed in forums and social media as a sign that a market bottom may be near.

Community Takeover (CTO) occurs when the original developers of a crypto project stop maintaining it and community members assume control of its channels or code. Community Takeover (CTO) is often associated with abandoned projects. Community Takeover (CTO) can expose holders to risks such as scams or manipulation when control passes to unverified parties.

Crypto Winter describes a prolonged bear market in which cryptocurrency prices fall for an extended period. Crypto Winter is marked by reduced investor interest and lower trading activity. Crypto Winter can lead to losses for consumers and to failures of projects that lack funding.

Cryptocurrency Money Laundering is the process of concealing the origin of illicit funds by moving them through digital assets. Cryptocurrency Money Laundering often uses techniques such as mixing services and transfers across multiple wallets to obscure transaction trails. Cryptocurrency Money Laundering exposes users to legal and financial risks when they interact with tainted funds.
